title: Airbus demonstrates Quantum-Secure communications in live tactical operations
source_used: EDR Magazine (text of an Airbus announcement); identical text also read at The Critical Communications Review
key_facts: Airbus Defence and Space says it has demonstrated a quantum-secure tactical communications network connecting military and law-enforcement users across different operational networks, which it calls a first.
The live trial took place in Malta on 10 and 11 Sep 2026 and was self-funded.
The architecture combined post-quantum cryptography (PQC, quantum-resistant algorithms) with quantum key distribution (QKD, physics-based secure key exchange) across multiple nodes.
Key management and software-defined networking (SDN) orchestrated encryption and routing as mission conditions changed.

At the centre was Agnet, Airbus's communication and collaboration platform; Merqury Cybersecurity supplied key management and SDN; Stormshield network encryptors and QKD from Telsy (a TIM Enterprise brand) via Quantum Telecommunications Italy ran over Melita's telecom infrastructure in Malta.
Airbus says the trial counters the 'harvest now, decrypt later' threat, where information intercepted today could be decrypted by future quantum computers.
No performance figures, user names or outside comment are given.
quote_evidence: Airbus Defence and Space has successfully demonstrated a quantum-secure tactical communications network connecting military and law enforcement users across different operational networks for the first time.
Conducted in Malta on the 10th and 11th September 2026, the self-funded live trial went beyond testing individual technologies.
The trial furthermore directly counters the critical “harvest now, decrypt later” threat, where sensitive information intercepted today could be decrypted by future quantum computers.
why_it_matters_hint: A defence supplier's field test of encryption meant to withstand future quantum computers, but every claim is Airbus's own.
event_date: Trial on 10 and 11 Sep 2026 in Malta; announced 5 Oct 2026.
notes: EDR Magazine (5 Oct 2026, 12:30 UTC) and The Critical Communications Review (5 Oct, 21:00 UTC) print identical text, which reads as an Airbus announcement; no independent comment, figures or user names. No earlier report of the trial found in a 21-day news search. Not carried in the previous 14 Full Reports.
